extracted.intended_audience: NASA public affairs officers, communications staff, and science communicators preparing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and checklist for drafting NASA press releases: required format elements, content components (lede, body, quotes), multimedia and boilerplate requirements, and scientific accuracy / public engagement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement with space exploration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize outreach and connection with the public as a core mission goal; craft content to draw audience interest in NASA activities and discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific accuracy non-negotiable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All scientific claims must be accurate and supported by underlying research; press releases should not overstate results. See Scientific Accuracy Standards for concrete checks (conclusions match papers, effect sizes given, limitations acknowledged, independent reviewer approval, authentic quotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspirational tone balanced with rigor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in an uplifting, motivational voice while preserving technical precision and not oversimplifying or sensationalizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia-rich to enable visual storytelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a variety of assets (images, video, animations, infographics) to support narrative and help audiences visualize missions and data; multimedia should reinforce scientific messages and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible language for broad audiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plain language over technical jargon; explain terms, use concrete examples and educational hooks so that the release is understandable to non-experts and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Header requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include NASA logo; 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' or embargo statement; release number (NA-XX-XXX); city and date. These elements are required metadata for official distribution and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline: Mission name + key finding/event; Active voice; 80 characters or less; News-first framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose a concise, news-first headline that leads with the mission or event and the key finding or announcement. Use active voice and keep within an 80-character limit for clarity and distribution compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede: Mission, finding, significance in 50 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening paragraph should state the mission, the main finding or event, and its significance in about 50 words. Include specific scientists, instruments, and dates where applicable and explain why it matters in a space science context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background on mission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise context about the mission’s purpose, history, objectives, and prior milestones so readers understand the significance of the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology of finding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize how the results were obtained (instruments, observations, analyses) at a high level sufficient for transparency without excessive technical detail; tie to the underlying paper or dataset when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote from project scientist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an authentic quote from a key scientist involved in the work to provide expert perspective and humanize the research; ensure quotes accurately reflect the science (see 'Author/scientist quote authentic').

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote from senior NASA official
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a quote from a senior NASA official to communicate organizational context, programmatic significance, or institutional priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what the finding means going forward: next steps, potential applications, follow-up missions or observations, and how it advances the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of partner organizations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and acknowledge partner institutions, international collaborators, and funding entities; this should appear in the body and/or credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-res images mandatory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-resolution, publication-quality images for use by media and outreach; images should be captioned and credited properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video b-roll if available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply video b-roll assets when possible to support broadcast and social coverage; include usage details and captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animation explainers when complex
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use animations to clarify complex concepts or processes that are difficult to convey with still images or text alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infographics for data-heavy stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear infographics to visualize data, effect sizes, timelines, or mission architectures for non-expert audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption credits proper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all multimedia have accurate captions and credit lines; include rights and usage statements where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a standard NASA boilerplate of ~50 words summarizing NASA's mission, the year founded (1958), budget context, and major current programs; keep boilerplate consistent across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions match underlying papers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the press release conclusions faithfully reflect the findings and claims made in the underlying peer‑reviewed papers or technical reports; do not overclaim or generalize beyond the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect sizes given fully
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effect sizes, magnitudes, or quantitative results with appropriate units and context so readers understand the scale and significance of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology summarized (scientific accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary of methods used to obtain the results to support transparency and reproducibility; link to full methods in the paper or technical release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations acknowledged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State important caveats, uncertainties, or limitations of the study so audiences and media do not misinterpret preliminary or uncertain results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent reviewer approval
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain review/approval from independent reviewers (internal/external subject-matter experts) to verify scientific accuracy before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/scientist quote authentic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that any quoted statements attributed to authors or scientists are accurate and approved by those individuals; avoid paraphrasing that changes meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language over jargon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor plain-language explanations and define unavoidable technical terms; write for broad public comprehension to maximize engagement and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete examples for abstract concepts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analogies or tangible examples to explain abstract scientific concepts so non-experts can grasp their meaning and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human interest angles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include human stories—scientists’ motivations, team challenges, or societal relevance—to increase reader connection and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational hooks for students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide elements that educators and students can use (e.g., classroom questions, learning links, links to educational resources) to extend the release into learning contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media kit included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a social media kit with suggested posts, images, short video clips, and hashtags to facilitate online dissemination and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NASA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consolidated checklist used to evaluate a release: Scientific accuracy verified; Multimedia comprehensive; Mission context clear; Quote from project scientist; Quote from NASA official; Plain language for accessibility; Educational hooks included; Acknowledgment of partners. Use this rubric to perform a final quality check before distribution.
